gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anek-kannada: Heavy Plakkaat letters curl their terminals almost back to the stem, closed up tight. And Anek Kannada, with terminals stopping well short, keeps paragraphs of sans text feeling open and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anek-odia: Contemporary Anek Odia keeps its rounds unlatched and friendly. Plakkaat hammers out heavy joints that never thin or bulge, and the body's capitals barely rise over its lowercase, so the two meet without fuss.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-chocolate-classic: Chocolate Classical Sans writes with a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, in a sizable lowercase. Yet Plakkaat, closed and cut like ribbon, makes the real difference against that open body.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-comme: Plakkaat draws its lines like bent straw, closed and heavy. Shrink it small and those closed shapes crowd, while Comme keeps its smooth sans curves clear at any size.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-cossette-texte: Clean, wide-eyed lowercase gives Cossette Texte its look, a clear foil to the closed, heavy Plakkaat. And its prominent x-height lets whole paragraphs flow along without strain, the n arches matching the stems.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-duru-sans: Plakkaat has no calligraphic modulation, just heavy letters bent like a single wire. Duru Sans then lets wide openings and dominant small letters carry the paragraphs smoothly, with ascenders barely showing.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans holds its stroke widths steady from stem to curve, with a lowercase e pried open. Funnel Sans handles quiet running text, while Plakkaat does its best work as a heavy, closed shout.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-hedvig-letters-sa: Approachable Hedvig Letters Sans leaves a wide gap where its c ends. Its small letters stand nearly as tall as capitals, so you can run it modestly small beneath the closed, heavy Plakkaat.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-kedebideri: Approachable and open, Kedebideri rounds its letters and lifts its x-height skyward. Kedebideri can be set a touch larger beside Plakkaat, since its open letters stay light against those closed, heavy ones.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-khula: Plakkaat letters look bent from a single wire, closed and heavy. Khula, a sans-serif with a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open, is the sharpest foil.
